title: Cost-Weighted RICE with Latency Elasticity — prototype scoring rubric
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Produce a practical, repeatable scoring rubric that augments traditional RICE with explicit cost and latency economics. The rubric should help product and GTM teams prioritize roadmap items where serving economics (per-token cost, latency SLOs) materially change the business case.

Motivation: Existing RICE implementations at Redwood emphasize reach and impact but underweight operational economics and latency risk for inference features (e.g., model upgrades, pipeline changes, caching, batching). As customers increasingly measure unit economics and tail latency, we need a prioritization input that surfaces trade-offs between product value and serving cost/latency.

Proposal summary: Extend RICE to include two additional multipliers: Cost Multiplier and Latency Elasticity. Compute a base RICE score (Reach * Impact * Confidence / Effort) and then apply adjustments that reduce the score when an item significantly increases unit cost or risks latency SLOs. The final prioritized_score is: 

prioritized_score = base_RICE_score * cost_factor * latency_factor * quality_adjustment

Where:
- cost_factor = 1 / (1 + normalized_expected_cost_increase) (bounded [0.5,1])
- latency_factor = 1 - P(latency_violation) * latency_penalty_weight (bounded [0.4,1])
- quality_adjustment = 1 - expected_quality_regression (if any)

Normalization: expected cost increase is expressed as percentage increase to per-token serving cost for the primary workload and is clipped at 100% for normalization. P(latency_violation) is estimated from engineering inputs (queueing model/back-of-envelope) and historical traffic shape.

Deliverables: prototype spreadsheet + scoring workbook, a one-page rubric doc for PMs and Eng, a small script to calculate scores from PRD fields, example scored backlog of 30 candidate initiatives, and a short playbook for cycle planning workshops.

Success criteria: rubric is adopted in at least two roadmap prioritization sessions during Cycle 48 and drives at least one re-prioritization where an initiative was deprioritized due to cost/latency risk.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype workbook created and verified with two real initiatives; 2) Eng provides latency risk estimates for those initiatives; 3) PMs run rubric in a planning workshop and log decisions; 4) Playbook published in Confluence and shared on Slack #pm-roadmap.
notes: Trade-off: multiplying by cost/latency reduces bias toward high-reach features that are expensive to serve — must guard vs. over-penalizing long-term strategic investments.
Boundaries: this rubric is for server-side inference features and infra-sensitive product changes; do not apply to non-serving UX work.
We should run sensitivity analysis across varying penalty weights and show the stability of top-10 picks.
